characterList.description: White female, long wavy brown hair, pale skin, wearing a patterned peach top. She is speaking to the camera, likely a vlogger.
characterList.name: Woman

characterList.description: Young male, short brown hair, large brown eyes, rosy cheeks, often wears a white shirt and blue shorts. He is a sea monster who can transform into a human.
characterList.name: Luca

characterList.description: Young male, curly brown hair, green eyes, freckles, often wears a yellow tank top and brown shorts. He is a sea monster who can transform into a human.
characterList.name: Alberto

characterList.description: Young female, short bright red curly hair in two buns, often wears a blue beanie, striped red and white shirt, and blue pants. She is a human girl.
characterList.name: Giulia

characterList.description: Adult male, large mustache, large chin, often wears a white sweater and a red and white striped apron, he also has a white cat on his shoulder. He is Giulia's father and a fisherman.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the fishing boat shown in the trailer?

qAndA.answer: The men are playing Scopa, a traditional Italian card game.
qAndA.question: What game are the men playing in the town square?

qAndA.answer: It's likely just a fun Easter egg connecting different Pixar films, not necessarily a narrative link.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the newspaper with Miguel from Coco on it?

qAndA.answer: Luca is nervous because the bike is clearly unsafe and Alberto's overconfidence makes Luca fear for their safety.
qAndA.question: Why is Luca nervous when riding the bike with Alberto?

qAndA.answer: The main conflict is the boys' struggle to keep their sea monster identities hidden from humans, particularly from Giulia's father who is suspicious and hates sea monsters. This conflict creates suspense and drives the narrative.

activities.description: Woman introduces the topic (breaking down the Luca trailer).
Panoramic shots of the Italian Riviera, focusing on a coastal town.
Close-up shot of a fishing boat named 'Elena'.
Shots of the town square filled with people.
Close-up of Luca taking in the sights.
Shots of town square with people, including men playing cards.
Shots of various stores and buildings in the town, including a seafood restaurant 'Bar Pittaluga'.
Close-up of Luca observing two kids eating watermelon.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The setting of the film is established as the Italian Riviera.
Luca observes two kids eating watermelon.

narrativeProgression.description: Establishing the setting of the film and introducing the main character, Luca.

props.name: Newspapers with image of Miguel from Coco.

activities.description: Close-up of Giulia.
Giulia talks to Luca and Alberto, they declare themselves 'underdogs'.

characterInteraction.description: Giulia appears confident and outgoing, Luca seems more shy and reserved, and Alberto is relaxed and smiling.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The three characters declare themselves 'underdogs' and join hands.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of Giulia and the bond formed between the three kids.

activities.description: Montage of various scenes: people drinking coffee, an Italian lady hanging laundry, Luca wandering around.
Luca and Giulia walking on rooftops at night.

characterInteraction.description: Giulia is leading the way, displaying her confidence and knowledge of the town, while Luca follows, appearing a little nervous.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Luca and Giulia explore the rooftops at night.

narrativeProgression.description: Highlighting the friendship between Luca and Giulia and their adventures in the town.

activities.description: Luca and Alberto stare longingly at the town from across the water.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Luca and Alberto yearn to be part of the town.

narrativeProgression.description: Suggesting a longing to belong and be part of the town, despite the dangers.

activities.description: Luca and Alberto building something.
Giulia talks to Luca and Alberto, they declare themselves 'underdogs' again.

characterInteraction.description: Alberto is confident and adventurous, while Luca remains hesitant. Giulia appears strong and assertive.

keyMoments.changeDescription: It's revealed that Luca has never been to Italy before.
It's revealed that Alberto is the one who drags Luca to the surface world.

narrativeProgression.description: Showcasing Alberto's influence on Luca, encouraging him to explore the human world, also hinting at potential conflict with Giulia's father.

activities.description: Luca and Giulia lying down looking at the stars.

characterInteraction.description: Giulia is talkative and animated, while Luca is quiet and observes her adoringly.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Luca is clearly enamored with Giulia.

narrativeProgression.description: Clearly establishing Giulia as the love interest.

activities.description: Luca and Alberto running down a hill.
Luca and Alberto jumping off a cliff into the water.
Luca and Alberto dancing, then transforming into sea monsters.

characterInteraction.description: Both boys are joyful and carefree, emphasizing their bond and shared secret.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The boys jump off a cliff, mirroring the concept art.
The boys transform into their sea monster forms.

narrativeProgression.description: Showcasing the joy and freedom the boys experience in both their human and sea monster forms.

activities.description: Luca and Alberto hiding from fishermen.
Montage of sea monsters being attacked by humans.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Luca states that their secret must stay hidden.
The fear of sea monsters is prevalent in the town.

narrativeProgression.description: Emphasizing the danger that sea monsters face from humans.

props.name: Drawings and a fountain depicting humans attacking sea monsters.

activities.description: Luca and Alberto swimming in the ocean, transforming into humans.
Luca and Alberto sitting at a table with Giulia and Massimo.

characterInteraction.description: Luca is anxious, Alberto is carefree until he partially transforms, Giulia seems oblivious, and Massimo is suspicious.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Luca and Alberto are having dinner with Giulia and her father.
Alberto accidentally transforms into a sea monster.
Massimo questions the boys about where they're from.

narrativeProgression.description: The climax of the trailer. The boys’ secret is almost revealed, creating tension and suspense.

props.name: Table, chairs, glasses of water, map of Italy with marked sea monster locations.

scenes.thematicElements: The dangers of hiding your true identity. The conflict between humans and sea monsters.
scenes.title: Facing the Fear

activities.description: Luca laughs nervously.

narrativeProgression.description: End of the trailer, leaving the audience wanting more.

activities.description: Woman wraps up the video, encourages viewers to like and subscribe.

climax.description: Alberto transforms into a sea monster in front of Giulia and her father.

storylines.description: The trailer presents a clear narrative with rising action, a climax, and a cliffhanger ending. It focuses on Luca and Alberto, two sea monsters who can transform into humans, as they explore the human world while trying to keep their true identities hidden.

The shot of Luca and Alberto staring at the town could be shortened, as the mood and message are already conveyed effectively in a shorter time frame.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello everyone and welcome back.
Today I'm going to be breaking down the Luca teaser trailer that was recently released.
To be completely honest, I first was a little unsure about this movie but the trailer
really sold the concept to me.
So the trailer opens up with a shot of the Italian ribby era.
There is beautiful blue water and lush green hills.
You can also see a town in the distance.
Next shot is the close up of the town and we see a fishing boat called Elena on the river.
As we will see as we go through this trailer, fishing will be a major element of the film.
After this we go into the town square filled with people and it looks exactly like Italy.
We previously saw a different angle of this shot in a promotional image as you can see
the same gelato and for cartridge store in the corner.
Another store that you can see is called Barbina Luca.
From the illustration it appears to be a seafood restaurant.
Next we get a close up of Luca taking in the science.
As you can see the character design is very cartoony, him having round features instead
of realistic ones.
The style also kind of reminds me of Walson Romant.
Next there is a group of men playing cards.
One of them yells out Scopal which is one of the two major national card games in Italy.
This is followed by some people enjoying coffee which is another part of the Italian culture.
Then we have that classic shot of an Italian lady hanging out the laundry that we have seen
in countless movies and TV shows set in Italy.
We get another shot of Luca wandering around and he comes across two kids eating a watermelon.
There is actually a cool little easter egg here with Miguel from Coco appearing on the
newspaper.
Next we get our first shot of Julia, the human girl character who again has a very cartoony
look with vibrant red hair.
As I previously said she looks very similar to Mae from the upcoming turning red and she
definitely has a similar personality to young Ellie from up.
Additionally it is important to note here that she is wearing a fisherman beanie which
makes sense as her father is a fisherman.
According to an entertainment weekly article Julia feels very righteous about injustice and
has this strong intensity.
My theory is that she is against the way her tan in Italy treats sea creatures, putting
her in conflict with her father.
In the next shot we see all three of the kid characters.
Their posture and facial expressions really sum up their personalities.
Julia looks strong and intense, Luca looks scared and insecure and Alberto looks confident
and carefree.
You might also notice that all of their feet are exposed which must have been a nightmare
to animate.
The three then declare themselves underdogs and they put their hands together cementing
their bond.
After this Italian version of you on my sunshine starts playing which I thought was a really
great choice.
More of the music plays we get four different shots of Julia and Luca walking on rooftops
at night.
Julia is leading the way as she knows the area and Luca is following behind her acting
shy.
I particularly like this shot of Julia helping Luca up and this shot of the moon is a
reference to director and Rico Casarosa's previous shot La Luna.
Next there is a shot of Luca and Alberto near the water staring longingly at the town.
This appears to be an emotional scene and hopefully we will be able to work out what is happening
when we get the plot information later.
This is a very revealing scene of Luca and Alberto building something.
Alberto has all of his clothing but Luca only has his seaweed shorts on which are part
of his similes to form as seen in the official poster.
From the entertainment weekly article we know that Alberto is the one who drags Luca to
the surface world.
He has been here before and has closed prepared.
In contrast it is Luca's first time in Italy and he doesn't have anything to wear yet.
After this we get another shot from the night sequence with Luca and Julia lying down.
Julia seems to be doing all of the talking giving off major Ellie vibes again.
In contrast Luca is sitting silently, looking at her lovingly.
It is quite clear from this shot that she is the love interest.
Now I know that a lot of people want Luca and Alberto to be together but I don't think
it's going to happen in this film.
The reason I think this is because the character of Luca is based on the director and Rico
Casarosa and Alberto is based on his real life childhood best friend.
These two people are not in a romantic relationship and on Rico is married to a woman.
I just don't think a person would base a character on themselves and then change their sexuality.
But I do hope we get a gay leading character in a Disney film soon as I think it's a great
idea.
Next is a shot of the two boys looking out to the water during sunset.
The coolest thing about this shot is that Luca has copied Alberto's hair.
Obviously he wants to be just like him.
Next we have several shots of the two friends running down a hill which we saw before at
the Disney investor day.
After this we have the C-Cave shot which we again have seen.
Next shot is new featuring Julia looking through a telescope while Luca is reading a book.
It is called Luneversa which translates to the universe.
This was the same book that Julia was holding earlier in the trailer which indicates that
she has a keen interest in exploring the world and could potentially get to explore the
C-Monks to world with the boys.
After this we get a shot of Luca and Alberto jumping off a cliff which is identical to
the first piece of concept art we got for the film.
Then we see Luca and Alberto dancing along to music played on a grammar phone.
This could potentially mean that the movie is not set in present day.
I haven't seen any modern technologies in this trailer so it could be set in the past.
An important thing to note here is that the plants on the floor are very unstable.
This could end in disaster as the boys could fall into the water exposing their c-Monks
to form.
Next sequence features Luca and Alberto on a bike which has clearly been handmade by
Alberto.
Luca looks pretty scared and is wearing a pot as a helmet.
You see Alberto thinks he is an expert on human things but he gets a lot of things wrong
as he is only looking at them from afar.
He is basically scuttle from the little mermaid.
This overconfidence causes him to make a bike that is clearly unsafe.
Also weirdly they have a life float on the back and I really don't think they need it.
They then fly off the ramp with a tortoise in front of it and go past some seagulls.
I'm fully expecting a finding Nemo Easter egg here.
Eventually they reach the water and we get our first look at the boys in their c-Monks
to form.
Alberto is a purple c-Monks out and Luca is a green and blue one.
Both have yellow eyes and pointy teeth.
They aren't super clear images but I expect we will get a better look in the next trailer.
We then have two randoms confused as to why two boys disappeared into the water.
I'm not sure if these characters will be significant to the plot or are just there for
this funny line.
The boys as seammonks are then seen hiding behind rocks from some fishermen.
Luca states that no one can find out and there is a montage of various images of humans
attacking seammonks with scary horror music playing.
The most significant image is of a fountain of a man slaying a seammonster who looks similar
to Massimo, possibly one of his ancestors.
The next shot features two angry old ladies holding gelato, presumably looking at Luca.
These were the same ladies seen in some of the concept art and they obviously hate seammonks.
After this we get a sequence of Luca and Alberto swimming in the ocean as they jump out of
the water they transform back into humans.
This was the moment I was sold on the whole seammonster thing, the transformation animation
was cool and I can't wait to see more.
We then get a new logo for the film which features the title Luca painted in blue and green
on a wall.
The end sequence is really cool and it actually reveals a lot about the film.
There is a horrifying shot of a fish being cut which reminds me of the chef's sequence
in the little mermaid.
The man cutting the fish is Julius father who has a tattoo depicting a seammonster being
killed so obviously he is going to be a major source of anxiety for the two boys.
Luca spits out his drink in horror causing half of Alberto's face to transform into a seamongster.
In a panic Luca throws him to the ground.
Luckily this goes unnoticed by Julia and her father but he does ask them where did you
boys say you were from?
Clearly suspicious of them.
I don't like how this character doesn't have eyes but I do really like the cat design.
It is quite obvious that this guy is out to get seammonks as to the left here is a
map of Italy with various locations of seammonks with no targets placed on them.
In an interview the director of the film said that seammonks are tied to Italian fishing
culture.
Fishmen would tell each other that there is a seamong saying there is a certain area
as there was good fishing there and they didn't want anyone else to go there.
And finally we have Luca laughing nervously at a title stating that the movie is coming
out summer 2021.
Anyway that is it for today.
Thank you so much for watching.
Like this video if you liked it and please subscribe.
It would mean so much to me.
Bye now and have a magical day.
